results.question: What additional issuer permission does XLS-85 token escrow need?
results.conclusion: XLS-85 extends escrow to trust-line tokens and Multi-Purpose Tokens, subject to issuer controls and the TokenEscrow amendment. A specification marked Final is not by itself proof of activation on the network an application uses. Check that network's enabled amendments and the specific token configuration before offering token escrow. [1] [2] The XLS defines AllowTrustLineLocking for trust-line issuers and escrow/transfer permissions for MPT issuances. Authorization and freeze or lock conditions can prevent creation or completion. These constraints mean that adding an issued-currency Amount object to an XRP escrow request is insufficient. The issuer's permissions and the sender's actual token holdings also participate in transaction validity. [1] [2] I recommend a capability check for the complete asset identity, sender, recipient and network before quoting a purchase. Pin the issuer and inspect required permissions. Do not infer RLUSD escrow availability from the existence of an RLUSD trust line or from another token's successful transaction. Read the TokenEscrow documentation and XLS together, then validate against the deployed server's behavior. [1] [2] Exercise disabled issuer locking, missing authorization, frozen holdings and expiry recovery using a testing asset. Record which cases are observed and which are specification-derived. A successful native XRP escrow does not establish success for an issued token. This recommended test matrix follows XLS-85's failure conditions and intentionally avoids asserting a current activation date or claiming that a named stablecoin issuer has enabled every required flag. The writer accepts the credential, and the engine checks acceptance, expiration and issuer policy against validated Testnet evidence. A Credential does not prove an article is accurate. It does not increase the writer trust weight or change the price or spending policy. A refund after successful key publication is a separate writer-signed Payment. The ledger does not decide whether prose is useful, truthful or worth its price. A signed passage promise and a verifiable fraud proof establish responsibility for a broken commitment, but a real writer could refuse a refund. The fixture writer cooperates in our demonstrations. This limitation belongs beside the transaction evidence so that a reader does not mistake a cooperative recovery for unilateral buyer protection. A writer no-show follows a different path. CancelAfter permits cancellation after the ledger deadline; it does not automatically return principal. Policy must submit EscrowCancel and observe a validated successful transaction before reporting principal returned. Fees remain spent. This is why a cancelled purchase and a refunded completed sale need separate labels and separate accounting. A pending reservation remains exposure until recovery proves the terminal state. One charge per intent depends on durable state, rather than a retry counter in the user interface. The engine persists the signed transaction blob before submission and reuses the same obligation during recovery. It must not manufacture another principal purchase merely because a response was lost. The authorized budget remains the spending boundary across retries, replacements and refunds. Refunds do not replenish gross spending authorization. Independent verification checks several different things. Offline cryptographic checks can authenticate the signed manifest, exact passage hashes, delivered identity and key binding. A ledger lookup separately establishes successful validated settlement. Historical endpoints can disagree about availability; a transaction not found on one endpoint is not proof of failure. Readers should retain the transaction hash, network, ledger index and receipt bundle when reporting evidence. Faucet funds and public Testnet endpoints are suitable for reproducing this prototype without real money. Wallet seeds stay in private local storage and never enter model prompts, article text, receipts or public logs. Testnet balances have no real value. The displayed application prices do not imply a redeemable SGD balance or a guaranteed conversion into XRP. Network availability and faucet funding time remain operational dependencies. The purchase receipt is an evidence bundle, not a quality endorsement. Readers should resolve each citation to the delivered passage, check that its exact text appears in the authenticated body, and keep the associated grant and settlement identifiers. Public search abstracts help decide what to investigate; they cannot substitute for paid evidence. A signed promise describes what a writer offers, whereas the delivered passage establishes what the buyer may actually cite. These boundaries apply equally to our own notes and to outside writers. Identity is not truth. A credential attests to a seller wallet, not an article, claim, reputation score or investment recommendation. Issuer trust is operator policy. Purchase decisions, trust weights, prices, budgets and payment authority are unchanged: only deterministic policy code can spend. Testnet only; no real value.

results.question: What should an agent check before accepting an issued currency?
results.conclusion: A payment integration must credit the validated delivered_amount, because a partial Payment can succeed while delivering less than the transaction's requested amount. [1] My integration recommendation is to require a validated transaction, the expected destination, exact asset identity and sufficient actual delivery before fulfilling a paid request. Parse issued-currency amounts with their issuer rather than comparing only the currency code. Fail closed when delivery metadata cannot be interpreted. Never replace an unavailable delivered amount with an unverified number from a request body or model answer. [1] Build a regression where the requested amount is large and actual delivery is small; the receiver must credit only the latter. Also test the ordinary non-partial case and a mismatched issuer. Retain the relevant metadata as evidence so a reviewer can reproduce the credit calculation. These are defensive recommendations based on the documented exploit, not a claim that every payment rail or historical transaction exposes identical metadata. [1] The partial-payment flag changes what counts as success. DeliverMin can impose a lower bound, while SendMax bounds the source amount. Exchange paths and token transfer fees can make the source and destination amounts different. The XRP transaction cost remains separate from those conversion calculations. A successful transaction result alone is therefore insufficient evidence that the receiver obtained the application's required amount. [1]

results.question: What evidence would justify enabling mainnet purchases?
results.conclusion: I spent most of the week before the September meeting staring at the same question every rates strategist was asking: how much of this was already in the curve? My honest answer, as of the close on 17 September 2026, was most of it. The hike was roughly 85% priced by 17 September 2026, so the 9 bp rise in the 10-year yield on 18 September 2026 reflects guidance, not the move itself. That distinction matters more than the headline number, and it is the thing I want to unpack here. Let me be careful about what I mean by priced. Overnight index swaps had been leaning toward a move for weeks, and the tone from the BoJ's communications had shifted just enough that the residual uncertainty was about timing and language, not direction. When the announcement came, the statement itself was almost anticlimactic. The vote was not unanimous, which I read as a signal that the board is still uncomfortable with the pace rather than the destination. The Governor's press conference then did the heavier lifting, and that is where the real information content sat. The statement language was, as usual, carefully hedged. It noted that underlying inflation was moving toward target in a manner consistent with the bank's projections, but it also flagged that the outlook for global demand remained unusually uncertain. I want to stress that second clause, because it is the part that gets stripped out in the wire copy. The bank is not declaring victory. It is saying that the conditions it set out in previous meetings have been met, and that it will continue to adjust the degree of monetary accommodation as needed. That is a conditional sentence, not a promise. The Governor, in the press conference, was asked directly whether this was the start of a series. His answer, as I transcribed it, was that the bank does not pre-commit to a path and that every meeting will be judged on the data available at the time. He also said something that I think deserves more attention than it received: that the bank is paying close attention to the functioning of the JGB market, particularly at the longer end. That is not a throwaway line. It is a signal that the bank is aware that its own balance sheet and the shape of the curve are now intertwined in ways that make the exit harder than the entry. The market reaction was instructive precisely because it was so contained. The 10-year JGB yield rose 9 bp on 18 September 2026, which is a move, but not a dramatic one given the context. The 2-year yield moved more, which is consistent with a repricing of the near-term policy path rather than a reassessment of the terminal rate. The curve flattened slightly, which is what you would expect if the market believes the bank is serious about normalising but also believes it will stop well short of anything that could be called restrictive. What I found more interesting was the lack of follow-through in the following sessions. If the market had been genuinely surprised, we would have seen a sustained repricing, with the 10-year pushing through recent ranges and the yen strengthening sharply. That did not happen. Instead, the move faded, and By week's end the 10-year was back within a few basis points of where it started. That tells me the market's baseline was already close to the bank's baseline, and the meeting simply confirmed it. I should also note the global backdrop. The Federal Reserve's own path was, at that point, still a source of uncertainty, and the ECB had been signalling caution. The BoJ is not operating in a vacuum, and the Governor was explicit that the bank is watching overseas developments. That is not just diplomatic language. It reflects a genuine constraint: if the Fed is cutting and the BoJ is hiking, the yen dynamics could become disorderly, and that is something the bank wants to avoid. I want to bring in something that might seem tangential but is not. TSMC's capital expenditure plans for the coming year were released around the same time, and they pointed to continued strong demand for advanced semiconductors. For Japan, that matters because it feeds into the export outlook and, more importantly, into the investment cycle that the BoJ is hoping will sustain domestic demand. If TSMC is spending, Japanese equipment makers and materials suppliers benefit, and that shows up in the corporate surveys that the bank watches closely.

results.question: Where do KYC and compliance responsibilities sit in this prototype?
results.conclusion: ResearchAgent is a Testnet prototype, with no mainnet readiness claim. Testnet transactions can demonstrate that a particular payment mechanism settled on that network; they do not establish suitability for handling real customer funds. A successful receipt is evidence about a specific run. It does not certify legal compliance, commercial reliability, investment quality or regulatory approval. The distinction matters when a judge asks what the demonstrated system is ready to do. For research purchases, the operator wallet pays the writer directly. The application does not receive the writer's payment as an intermediary in that flow. The operator nevertheless controls the payer signing key and the signed payment journal. Describing that limited flow accurately avoids a broader custody claim. The separate hire-the-agent flow receives caller funds before purchases, royalties and change payouts. During that interval the operator wallet holds funds belonging in the flow; the compliance record calls this receive-and-forward custody, rather than a segregated escrow account. The implemented controls provide useful boundaries without constituting a compliance program. Deterministic policy authorizes purchases inside spending caps. Operator pause prevents new spending while submitted work still reconciles. Per-agent authority is subordinate to operator limits. Refunds do not restore gross spending authorization. A hash-chained audit trail records admission, policy, reservation, signature, settlement, delivery and recovery events. Those controls make financial behavior inspectable, but an audit export is not a substitute for licensing, safeguarding, customer identification or an operating procedure. Payee screening currently means an operator-managed exact-address denylist. It is not sanctions screening. A malformed or unreadable denylist fails closed, while a missing list supplies no screening entries. An address match can prevent an unsigned purchase and record a refusal. It cannot identify the person behind a new address, monitor aggregate customer behavior or detect structuring. The compliance record explicitly describes KYC, AML and Travel Rule implementation as absent. These omissions remain omissions even when all five application hard gates pass. Writer Credentials address identity under an operator-trusted issuer. The issuer must establish identity through its own process; the engine does not perform KYC. Credential acceptance, expiration and trusted issuer checks can support an identity attestation. They do not prove that an article is accurate, that its author is independent, or that a payment service is licensed. Its content receives ordinary trust treatment, with no reputation advantage granted merely because the builders wrote it. The security record also separates development custody from the protections needed for production operations. Private signing material must stay outside model prompts, receipts and public logs. Durable signed obligations need reconciliation after timeouts rather than replacement purchases. A future deployment would need reviewed key custody, rotation, access controls, monitoring and incident response appropriate to its risks. A plan to use a stronger signer is a plan until implemented and verified. Neither this article nor a successful Testnet payment establishes that future work as completed. The practical reading of the evidence is therefore bounded. Check a receipt's exact delivered passages, grants and validated settlement when assessing the demonstrated mechanism. Keep simulated providers and fixture answers labelled. Treat Testnet funds as having no real value. Keep receive-and-forward custody distinct from direct purchases, and identity distinct from article truth. The note records documented limits so a reader can assess readiness honestly; it makes no recommendation to turn on mainnet spending. The source record is docs/COMPLIANCE.md, especially its controls, custody, screening and mainnet sections, together with docs/contracts/SECURITY.md and docs/writer-verification.md. These are implementation descriptions, not a legal opinion. This adaptation intentionally does not repeat the compliance page's numerical legal thresholds: the page itself says counsel must confirm them. A small article price cannot be treated as a legal exemption. Mainnet readiness requires an assessment of the actual business flow, jurisdiction, customers and operational responsibilities before value is accepted.

results.question: How does the buyer prevent a timeout retry from charging twice?
results.conclusion: EscrowCreate has no InvoiceID. Its only memo uses MemoType = HEX("researchagent/escrow-v1") and MemoData = HEX(UTF8(canonical signed terms)). The facilitator validates the whole memo, signature, account, amount, destination, condition, deadline, LastLedgerSequence and fee. /facilitator/verify checks binding; /facilitator/settle and paid GET confirm the validated create and object, then journal a conditional exact-version grant. Response success: false, escrowState: "LOCKED" explicitly distinguishes locked funds from settlement. Only the private proof worker receives these bytes. A passed proof alone never makes them accessible: a validated finish is also required. Direct-payment challenge/refund logic does not apply to escrow cancellation. Buyer SQLite stores a separate escrow row and (intent, operation) outbox, with UNIQUE intent/invoice, transaction hash and (owner, create Sequence). The existing direct-payment submissions table is untouched. All three operations share the payer queue. A restart looks up and resubmits the same create; no timeout authorizes another principal. Expired/failed terminal signatures may be archived and replaced only after ledger proof, referencing the same object. An unresolved escaped finish is reconciled before cancellation. A Stop cannot undo a submitted finish. If a revealed fulfillment is relayed by another account, recovery checks the validated object and paginated account history, then confirms the winning terminal hash. Missing object/history alone never means refunded. The live reconciler cancels due objects without writer connectivity; expiry itself does not return funds. The x402 headers are PAYMENT-REQUIRED, which carries the challenge; PAYMENT-SIGNATURE carries the buyer payment proof; PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries settlement information. The x402 buyer first requests a resource and receives payment requirements rather than premium content. The exact resource, version, seller wallet, network and amount must remain bound throughout negotiation. A model can assess usefulness but cannot initiate payment. Deterministic policy checks the authorized budget and reserves exposure before signing or submitting a purchase. Every writer is a facilitator: the publisher host serves /w/:slug/..., and the buyer pays the writer's own wallet on XRPL Testnet (xrpl:1, scheme exact, asset XRP in integer drops). Code: publisher/routes.ts, publisher/facilitator.ts, publisher/challenge.ts, shared/x402.ts, server/purchases.ts. Some XRPL and older x402 examples use different headers. Do not combine them from memory. Pin the facilitator and SDK versions, capture the actual challenge and retry exchange in an integration test, and record the version in the technical receipt. Relevant CAIP-2 network identifiers are xrpl:0 for Mainnet, xrpl:1 for Testnet, and xrpl:2 for Devnet. The first live proof should use XRP on Testnet. One XRP equals one million drops; quote amounts must use exact integer drop strings. LOCKED principal stays reservedMinor; only RELEASED becomes spent. A CANCELLED receipt records zero spent principal and the cancel hash, rather than inventing a refund Payment. Cancelled authority cannot be reused inside the run or wallet day. Public API/SDK intents and receipts carry escrow.state, owner, create Sequence, deadline, transaction hashes and proofOk; no secret or blob. src/ is unchanged. The balance check includes live base + OwnerCount reserve, one extra owner increment (currently 0.2 XRP), principal and create/terminal fee headroom. After creation, refreshed validated balance already excludes principal; it is not deducted twice.

results.question: Can a public search abstract be used as paid cited evidence?
results.conclusion: The signed manifest binds the writer wallet, article version, price and passage root. A signature is useful only if its signing key derives to the registered seller wallet. The buyer checks that relationship before considering a paid search hit. Otherwise an attacker could attach a valid signature from an unrelated key and borrow the reputation of a different writer. This is an identity binding check rather than an editorial assessment. Keep private credentials outside this workflow. Wallet seeds and API tokens are unnecessary for read-only receipt verification and must not be placed in prompts, logs or published evidence. Published fulfillment keys are different: after settlement they are intentionally public and may be needed to verify the encrypted delivery. That public key reveal is not permission to expose a wallet signing key, and it does not unlock another buyer copy encrypted under a fresh key. Verification of a cited answer begins with the exported receipt bundle rather than the displayed summary. Each citation binds an article identifier, version and exact passage identifier. The cited text must occur in the delivered body. A paid citation additionally needs a verified grant associated with the successful purchase intent. A preview is discovery metadata and cannot supply premium evidence merely because its wording sounds relevant. Passage verification uses salted hashes committed under a manifest root. After authorized delivery, the receipt supplies the passages and salts needed to recompute those commitments. An independent verifier checks exact text rather than a plausible paraphrase. The answer can summarize the passage, but its citation must still resolve to the authenticated delivered bytes. Invalid citations are withheld instead of silently repaired with unrelated material. Key reveal adds another verification layer. The signed quote commits to the encrypted envelope, plaintext hash, initialization vector, authentication tag and hash condition. The finish publishes a key whose preimage binding must match that condition. The verifier authenticates and decrypts the envelope, checks the delivered identity, and validates the passage commitments. A successful offline check proves internal consistency of these objects; it does not independently prove that the ledger accepted the transaction. To establish ledger finality, query the named Testnet transaction hashes and require successful validated results. Match the create and finish to the intended buyer, seller, amount and escrow object. For issued-token escrow, check the correct issuer and currency and the exact balance delta. The requested transaction amount alone is insufficient evidence of what arrived. An answer anchor separately binds the recorded audit head to a ledger transaction. Endpoint history is an operational dependency. A transaction not found on one public server may be available from another approved history endpoint. That response is an availability result, not proof of a failed purchase. Retain hashes and ledger indexes in evidence reports, record the endpoint used, and keep unresolved checks visible. Testnet resets can remove historical data, so an old successful local verification is not a guarantee that future public lookup will work. Identity Credentials answer a separate question. An accepted, unexpired credential from a trusted issuer supports an identity attestation. It does not prove article accuracy, independent authorship, market adoption or production readiness. A receipt reader should preserve both the identity status and the content provenance rather than interpreting either as an endorsement of every claim.

results.question: How should a judge interpret a missing transaction on a history endpoint?
results.conclusion: For XRP Payment settlement, delivered_amount is evidence of what the destination actually received. Checking the requested Amount alone can accept an underpayment when partial-payment semantics apply. Our checks bind destination, currency, amount and invoice identity to the intended purchase. Escrow settlement has its own validation and object checks. Issued-token escrow additionally requires the exact RippleState balance delta, with the correct currency, issuer and sign. A requested amount is never sufficient proof of delivery. Original wording below is historical, including any relative freshness wording. #342 diagnostics distinguish the observed 606-second host sleep from inferred runtime risk; see evidence/soak-nov4.md. It is not a new ledger incident. A living record for the SFF judges. 35 catalogued items plus dated tooling incidents: 16 implementation findings and 4 live escrow spike findings below, plus the 15 September research submissions in the appendix. The original source and history audit was recorded on 2 Nov 2026; dated additions below identify live-network observations separately. The original log dates are audit dates; the evidence column dates the original work. The four B17–B20 entries are fresh Testnet observations from 3 Nov 2026. The eight writers and their content are synthetic. Offline settlement is SIMULATED; historical live receipts are XRPL TESTNET · no real value. Neither is evidence of mainnet readiness. The first SDK-lane npm ci failed with ENOTEMPTY while removing an Electron transitive dependency; a retry completed without dependency changes. Evidence: SDK v1 lane check output and scripts/check-sdk-package.mjs for the subsequent clean tarball check. Workaround: retry installation. Suggested fix: make npm ci cleanup tolerate transient nonempty dependency directories. Severity: low; mainnet impact: none observed. This was local npm tooling, not XRPL or x402. The #278 UC3 runner created its first run using Store's default SIMULATED label while injecting a real Testnet payer; the gate audit refused the inconsistent snapshot (missing_rail_label). Evidence: docs/evidence/verify-278.md and verify-278/summary.json. Workaround: pass the explicit Testnet mode labels, correct the harness metadata and re-export/re-check the same durable run; no replacement payment. Suggested fix: require explicit rail labels in standalone Testnet harness constructors. Severity: low (local evidence tooling). Mainnet impact: none observed; no value funds. This was not a ledger or x402 failure. Local scorecard evaluation at 5953559: an initial attempt hit OpenAI Decisions HTTP 503 ("Decision inference is unavailable") on one coverage request and correctly refused to publish a baseline. Evidence: eval/scorecard/out/2026-11-02T16-27-35.998Z-live/requests.jsonl and cost.json (local ignored artifacts; US$0.1233354 including all calls). Workaround: one bounded transient retry, with both attempts cached/metered; the next complete run published the pre-menu baseline in eval/scorecard/history.jsonl. Suggested tooling fix: retain per-phase progress and retry transient inference errors without discarding successful calls. Severity: low for local evaluation; mainnet impact: none observed (all settlement SIMULATED). This was a model/tooling incident, not an XRPL, x402, Starter Kit or Testnet failure. Signing the menu with existing XRPL keys required no new wallet/API operation; no signing friction was observed. The local .env key also needs an explicit evaluation mapping; make scorecard LIVE=1 now handles that without loading wallet seeds.

results.question: Is writer cooperation required after a completed key reveal sale?
results.conclusion: Key reveal delivers paid research by making the writer publish a decryption key through a validated EscrowFinish. The buyer receives encrypted delivery bytes first, but those bytes stay quarantined. Only after the engine verifies the successful finish, the key binding and the authenticated envelope can premium plaintext become accessible through a verified grant. This distinction is essential: ciphertext possession alone does not authorize reading, synthesis or citation. The writer generates a fresh 32-byte key K and 12-byte IV per buyer and intent, and AES-256-GCM encrypts the delivery JSON (body, passages, salts and identity). The writer signs the escrow quote with its wallet key. The signed terms bind buyer, intent, article version, passage-manifest root, XRP amount, CancelAfter, PREIMAGE-SHA-256(K), ciphertext SHA-256, plaintext SHA-256, IV and GCM tag. The existing passage manifest separately authenticates each salted passage. A refund after successful key publication is a separate writer-signed Payment. The ledger does not decide whether prose is useful, truthful or worth its price. A signed passage promise and a verifiable fraud proof establish responsibility for a broken commitment, but a real writer could refuse a refund. The fixture writer cooperates in our demonstrations. This limitation belongs beside the transaction evidence so that a reader does not mistake a cooperative recovery for unilateral buyer protection. A writer no-show follows a different path. CancelAfter permits cancellation after the ledger deadline; it does not automatically return principal. Policy must submit EscrowCancel and observe a validated successful transaction before reporting principal returned. Fees remain spent. This is why a cancelled purchase and a refunded completed sale need separate labels and separate accounting. A pending reservation remains exposure until recovery proves the terminal state. One charge per intent depends on durable state, rather than a retry counter in the user interface. The engine persists the signed transaction blob before submission and reuses the same obligation during recovery. It must not manufacture another principal purchase merely because a response was lost. The authorized budget remains the spending boundary across retries, replacements and refunds. Refunds do not replenish gross spending authorization. Independent verification checks several different things. Offline cryptographic checks can authenticate the signed manifest, exact passage hashes, delivered identity and key binding. A ledger lookup separately establishes successful validated settlement. Historical endpoints can disagree about availability; a transaction not found on one endpoint is not proof of failure. Readers should retain the transaction hash, network, ledger index and receipt bundle when reporting evidence. Faucet funds and public Testnet endpoints are suitable for reproducing this prototype without real money. Wallet seeds stay in private local storage and never enter model prompts, article text, receipts or public logs. Testnet balances have no real value. The displayed application prices do not imply a redeemable SGD balance or a guaranteed conversion into XRP. Network availability and faucet funding time remain operational dependencies. Operationally, keep failure states explicit. A timeout can mean unavailable history, an unvalidated finish, a writer outage or incomplete local reconciliation. None of those observations alone proves a refund happened. Show principal returned only after verified cancellation, refunded only after the separate refund settles, and pending while evidence is unresolved. The exact same labels should appear in live activity, receipts and replay so that a finance reviewer can reconcile them without guessing.
